facts.raw_span: A 34-year-old woman
gravida 2 para 1
previous cesarean section
presented at 4 weeks 5 days of amenorrhea
1-day history of epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen
denied fever, nausea, vomiting, or vaginal bleeding
afebrile, hemodynamically stable
epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs were negative
white blood cell count of 13.54×10^9/L
β-hCG level of 523 IU/L
empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness

concepts.why: The presence of epigastric tenderness and a high white blood cell count could indicate an ovarian cyst or torsion.

support_spans: β-hCG level of 523 IU/L
empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness
contradict_spans: epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
concepts.why: The presence of a high β-hCG level and an empty uterus could indicate a corpus luteum cyst, although the epigastric tenderness is not typical.

support_spans: epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
